script_bugs_found_and_fixed: B2: inspect_btn.count() was checked before the Lab operations dialog had rendered past its 'Checking what this VM can do...' placeholder; fixed with locator.wait_for(state='visible').

B2: the /api/operations poller assumed a dict-with-'items' response shape and called .get() on it before checking isinstance, crashing on the real (bare list) response; fixed to branch on isinstance first.
B3: cEOS's terminal starts in the unprivileged ceos> prompt; 'configure' alone is refused ('Invalid input (privileged mode required)'); fixed by sending 'enable' first.

B3: the Progress tab status-text selector assumed a '.badge' class that does not exist in git-progress.js's real markup (gitRenderSaves uses '<details class="git-saved-job"><summary><span class="pill">...'); fixed to read the <summary> text of the newest 'details.git-saved-job'.

B3: one push attempt landed in push_pending with 'Another Git operation is already running for this repository' (host_git.py Repository.lock, a real VM-side advisory flock, most likely held briefly by a concurrent repository-status check); this was not a script bug, so it was retried through the product's own 'Upload now' retry action (added a bounded retry loop) rather than worked around out of band; it succeeded on the very next Save progress attempt, and the original stuck job later resolved itself to 'synced' on its own.

C1 and C3: assumed the topology browser (browse()) would list the annotations file beside the topology; host_operations.py browse() (line 131) deliberately lists only directories and *.clab.yaml/*.clab.yml files (the dialog's own 'Only topology files are listed' text, enforced server-side too) -- this is by design, not a defect. Reproduced independently with a throwaway curl-only create+delete cycle against a scratch file (qa42-curl-test.clab.yaml, created and then removed again through the manager's own reviewed create/delete actions) before concluding it was a false FAIL in the check, not a missing write. Fixed the check to confirm the annotations file through the read route instead.

C2: with a blank draft already open, dropping a pair triggers the native confirm('Replace the current draft with the dropped lab?'), which Playwright auto-dismisses (returns false) unless a dialog handler is armed, silently cancelling the drop; fixed by dropping directly on the fresh welcome page's own drop zone (#builder-drop) before starting any draft, which also matches the brief's literal wording ('start a blank lab' = the builder's blank initial state) and armed a defensive dialog-accept handler regardless.

C2: '.react-flow__node' also counts the map's text/shape/group annotation nodes, not just topology devices (13 devices + 6 free-text + 3 free-shape + 4 group-style + edge-label nodes = 27); fixed to count '.react-flow__node-topology-node' (the same node-type class map-editor-page.js itself reads for its own selected-node lookup).

C3: publish/revise operate purely against the VM file path and never touch My labs, so after publishing then revising directly (without ever opening the saved file's own dialog), there was nothing registered in My labs for '#remove-lab' to remove, and the goto_home()/lab-card wait timed out; fixed by inserting the normal 'Add to My labs without starting' step (from the topology-file dialog opened via #op-open-published) right after publish succeeds. Because the main script run had already published and revised the qa42-builder folder before this fix, the add/remove pair was completed with two small standalone follow-up scripts against that same already-published folder rather than re-running the whole builder flow from scratch (which would have collided with the folder already on the VM).

D: #capture-prepare stayed disabled because no interface checkbox was ever ticked (only the target device was selected); fixed by explicitly checking eth1, matching the approach already used successfully in the 1.30.39 QA tool.
